_comment: Buildings inside settlements (DESIGN §3.3). Every building needs 'hands' to run; staffing is linear (half staff = half effect). 'mandatory' buildings exist from founding and cannot be demolished; they are per tier ('tier'). Every other building is built by the player (Session 11, DECIDED by Omer 2026-11-05): 'minTier' is the lowest tier that may build it; 'cost' is paid when the project is queued — 'money' from the faction treasury (DESIGN §4.2b; Omer 2026-11-05 Session 12c: prices ×5 the first draft, so a town of ~10,000 affords a modest building every 2–3 years from its own tax and the realm's whole income buys a few a year), 'timber' and 'stone' from the CLUSTER stockpile (DESIGN §4.2); construction then takes 'buildMonths' months with 'buildHands' spare/private hands (fewer hands → proportionally slower; in a town or city the hands on the site pay no tax); 'requires' names a hex the settlement must work (river / shore / pasture). 'effects' are read by src/sim/economy.ts: farmingBonus and fishingBonus multiply those outputs (× staffing); granaryCapacityMonths adds months of capacity and granarySpoilageMult multiplies spoilage; goodsMult multiplies the goods the settlement's PRIVATE hands make (Workshop — a multiplier, not an employer, Omer Session 11b); salesShare is the share of the cluster's goods the settlement sells a year (Market — the only way goods become money, Omer Session 12c); stockCap raises the cluster's stockpile cap (Warehouse); order and unlocks are recorded only — order has no effect until DESIGN §4.4 exists and unlocks (recruitment) waits for Phase 4. Names of the village hall and the metropolis hall are PLACEHOLDERS (DESIGN §5), so is 'Drill Yard'. All numbers are DRAFT, at MODEL SCALE ×3 (see data/economy.json modelScale): hall 30/150/300/600, granary 90/180/360/720.

buildings.name: Mill
buildings.blurb: Grinds the harvest of the whole settlement: +15 % farming output. Needs a river hex in the work zone.

buildings.name: Great Granary
buildings.blurb: Stone-built stores: +12 months of granary capacity, spoilage halved.

buildings.name: Fishing Wharf
buildings.blurb: Boats and drying racks: +50 % fishing output. Needs a shore, lake or river hex in the work zone. Later the port that reaches offshore fish.

buildings.name: Workshop
buildings.blurb: Guild wardens and a shared hall for the town's artisans: the private hands make +50 % more goods into the cluster's stockpile.

buildings.name: Market
buildings.blurb: Stalls, tolls and a weighing house: sells 60 % of the cluster's goods a year into the realm's treasury. Without a Market, goods only pile up (Omer, Session 12c).

buildings.name: Chapel
buildings.blurb: Raises public order (+5) — recorded only, until public order exists (DESIGN §4.4).

buildings.name: Warehouse
buildings.blurb: Sheds and a stone cellar: the cluster's stockpile holds +900 timber, +450 stone and +450 goods more before the rest flows to the realm.

buildings.name: Archery Range
buildings.blurb: Trains archers. Recruitment comes with Phase 4.

buildings.name: Stables
buildings.blurb: Horses for mounted units. Needs a pasture hex in the work zone (DESIGN §3.1). Recruitment comes with Phase 4.

buildings.name: Drill Yard
buildings.blurb: Trains melee levies (PLACEHOLDER name). Recruitment comes with Phase 4.

buildings.name: Palisade
buildings.blurb: Wooden wall. Effect comes with Phase 4.

buildings.name: Walls
buildings.blurb: Stone walls. Effect comes with Phase 4 (sieges).

buildings.name: Barracks
buildings.blurb: Professional recruitment. Effect comes with Phase 4.

buildings.name: Ironworks
buildings.blurb: Armour and weapons. Effect comes with Phase 4.

buildings.name: Citadel
buildings.blurb: The strongest fortification. Effect comes with Phase 4.
